doc.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

title: Reform school and school brass bands
summary: Pops sweeping at the reform school band; Mugsy starting on bass drum at a training school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: It was funny back then, the reform school. I should have been under that reform school. I used to go back there and help them guys sweep out that long hall so they could hit the rehearsal of the band. Did you play with that band? I tried to play bass drum. I tried everything back there with them. I'd do my dirt, man. Get up a little bit more and go back to Jones' home. Walk by that long walk, too. Where were you yesterday all day at Jones' home, what you was doing out there, sweeping up the rehearsal of the band, and call up there and ask you what you said all day. Well, I'm clear of that.
I used to like to play the brass band. I started out as a drummer recently.

Really? You know, all your best swing trumpet players, all your best trumpet players, that they fight, it doesn't care how much the horn they play when they play with the brass band, the old guys, the first thing they put on is bass drum.
Did they have brass bands in Chicago?
